derivations.quote: Given a physical input $f$, call $g=D_{\rm in}^{-1}f$ its logical interpretation. The claim is that at every vertex $v$ the stored array equals $D_v$ applied to the logical array there.

If the scalar network is a signed role permutation sending input role $w$ to output role $\rho(w)$ with sign $\varepsilon_w$, the route of $w$ applies $\varepsilon_wD_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))}D_{\mathrm{source}(w)}^{-1}$ to its array.

relations.quote: A frame is an invertible linear operator attached to each vertex of a network whose wires carry arrays instead of scalars; it lets the [Linear exchange network with restored scratch wires](linear-network.md) run on arrays so that only the two endpoint frames affect the result, and each edge pays only for a change of frame.
Later pages measure edge cost by the rank of the change, using [Rank, subspaces and orthogonal complements](linear-algebra-basics.md).

symbols.name: scalar ring
symbols.meaning: The ring of scalars of the network.
symbols.quote: Let $R$ be the ring of scalars of the network and $\Omega$ a finite set of addresses shared by all wires.

symbols.name: address set
symbols.meaning: The finite set of addresses indexing the entries of each wire's array.
symbols.quote: Let $R$ be the ring of scalars of the network and $\Omega$ a finite set of addresses shared by all wires.

symbols.name: array network
symbols.meaning: The network obtained by applying each scalar gate pointwise at every address of the arrays.
symbols.quote: Write $\mathsf S_\Omega$ for the resulting network.

symbols.name: frame
symbols.meaning: The invertible R-linear operator on R^Omega assigned to vertex v.
symbols.quote: Each source, gate and sink $v$ gets an invertible $R$-linear operator $D_v$ on $R^\Omega$, its frame.

symbols.name: input frame
symbols.meaning: The direct sum over roles of the source frames.
symbols.quote: Let $D_{\rm in}$ and $D_{\rm out}$ be the direct sums of the source frames and of the sink frames over the roles.

symbols.name: output frame
symbols.meaning: The direct sum over roles of the sink frames.
symbols.quote: Let $D_{\rm in}$ and $D_{\rm out}$ be the direct sums of the source frames and of the sink frames over the roles.

symbols.name: physical input
symbols.meaning: The array actually supplied to the sources.
symbols.quote: Given a physical input $f$, call $g=D_{\rm in}^{-1}f$ its logical interpretation.

symbols.name: logical input
symbols.meaning: The logical interpretation D_in^{-1} f of the physical input.
symbols.quote: Given a physical input $f$, call $g=D_{\rm in}^{-1}f$ its logical interpretation.

symbols.name: route sign
symbols.meaning: The sign of the route sending input role w to output role rho(w).
symbols.quote: If the scalar network is a signed role permutation sending input role $w$ to output role $\rho(w)$ with sign $\varepsilon_w$, the route of $w$ applies $\varepsilon_wD_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))}D_{\mathrm{source}(w)}^{-1}$ to its array.

symbols.name: role permutation
symbols.meaning: The map sending each input role w to its output role rho(w).
symbols.quote: If the scalar network is a signed role permutation sending input role $w$ to output role $\rho(w)$ with sign $\varepsilon_w$, the route of $w$ applies $\varepsilon_wD_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))}D_{\mathrm{source}(w)}^{-1}$ to its array.
